I felt this sick, cold dread in my chest because the only reason my CGPA is high is that our exams were mostly MCQs and I got lucky with my guesses on the tough math sections. I'm not smart, I'm just incredibly good at taking tests, and the thought of trying to clear actual technical interviews where I have to explain concepts out loud makes me want to drop out.

The department head just nominated me for the outstanding student researcher award, and instead of being happy, I'm having a full-blown panic attack. I spent the last hour looking at the abstract of my paper thinking it's completely surface-level and that the peer-reviewers must have been asleep when they accepted it. I feel like a total thief of opportunities that should have gone to actual geniuses in my batch who spend 14 hours a day in the lab.

I just got placed at a tier-1 firm with a 24 LPA package, and honestly, I feel like vomiting. My friend who literally taught me dynamic programming during the prep weeks got rejected in the resume round, and here I am, someone who barely cleared the cut-off, getting the offer letter. Every time someone congratulates me on the group chat, I feel like a filthy thief who stole someone else's life.

My CGPA came out to 9.2 this semester, but I can't even celebrate. I literally guessed on three of the hardest MCQs in the OS midterm and happened to get them right, and the prof graded my final project so leniently compared to others. Everyone thinks I'm some coding prodigy, but the truth is I struggle to write a basic recursive function without StackOverflow, and I’m terrified the next lab exam is going to completely expose how incompetent I actually am.

They made me the technical lead for the college web-dev club, and I feel like an absolute clown. The juniors come to me asking about system architecture and AWS hosting, and inside, I'm screaming because I just watch YouTube tutorials ten minutes before the meet to look smart. I am living in constant panic that one of these brilliant freshmen is going to ask a question I can't answer and everyone will realize I'm just a fraud pretending to know how to code.

Our team won second place in the hackathon last weekend, but I literally did nothing but build the frontend UI using basic CSS templates while my teammates did all the heavy lifting with ML models. Now they're sharing the project on LinkedIn and tagging me as a 'genius collaborator'. I feel so dirty and ashamed reading those comments because I know deep down I was just dead weight they dragged to the finish line.

My guide praised my research draft in front of the whole seminar group today, saying it had 'excellent analytical depth'. I wanted the ground to swallow me whole because half the papers I cited were things I barely skimmed, and I used ChatGPT to polish the abstract. I feel like a con artist who scammed a highly respected professor, and every time he emails me now, my stomach drops because I think this is the email where he tells me he found out I'm a fake.

Got my grades back for the advanced DSA class and somehow ended up with an A-. I literally felt sick to my stomach because I guessed on like half the tree-traversal questions and code-traced like a headless chicken. Everyone in our batch WhatsApp group is talking about their solid 9+ CGPA and I'm sitting here waiting for the day my professor realizes I can't even write a basic heap sort from scratch without copying GitHub gists. I don't belong here, it was all luck.

Just cleared the technical round for a massive software company and my dad immediately called everyone in our family to brag about the 'upcoming 40 LPA package'. I literally feel like a complete scam. I only got the internship because the interviewer asked me the exact sliding window question I memorized the night before on LeetCode. If they hire me and hand me a real production codebase, I'm going to freeze and get fired on day one.

My teammate in the capstone project is a literal coding god who does everything in his sleep, and I just sit there during meetings nodding along pretending I understand the architecture diagrams. When we won the department showcase yesterday, I wanted to crawl under the desk and disappear. They gave me equal credit on the certificate but I spent the entire weekend crying because I know I contributed absolutely nothing of value compared to him.

My LinkedIn feed is just a graveyard of my own self-esteem with everyone posting 'thrilled to share' updates about their summer internships. I finally got an offer from a decent mid-sized startup, but I can't even celebrate. I keep thinking they only picked me because they had a diversity quota or because they ran out of other candidates. I'm terrified that when I show up for the onboarding, they'll realize they made a huge mistake and revoke the offer.

I was nominated for the student representative council because our professor liked my presentation, but I am literally paralyzed with dread. I'm just a quiet kid who stays in the back row and copies notes from friends because I'm too slow to understand lectures in real-time. If I accept this leadership role, everyone is going to see how incredibly disorganized and clueless I actually am when it comes to managing anything.

I just got the offer letter for the Amazon SDE intern role, and instead of being happy, I’m throwing up in the bathroom. I literally only solved the coding rounds because the interviewer asked the exact two DP questions I memorized the night before. If they had asked literally anything else, I would have failed on the spot. I’m starting in a month and I’m terrified they're going to realize I'm a complete fraud who doesn't even understand basic system design.

Everyone is congratulating me for getting a 9.4 CGPA this semester, but it feels like a sick joke. My university’s grading system is incredibly lenient, and I just know how to memorize PPTs the night before exams to get marks. In the labs, I literally just copy-paste boilerplate code and pray it compiles, while my batchmates are building compiler engines from scratch. I feel like a parasite sucking up praise I don't deserve, and the fall from grace is going to kill me when actual placements start.

I was made the lead for our college hackathon team because I'm the senior, but I am so out of my depth it's not even funny. The sophomores on my team are writing clean, asynchronous Node.js code like it's breathing, and I'm sitting here struggling to debug a basic CORS error. I keep assigning myself 'managerial tasks' just to hide the fact that I don't know how to code my way out of a paper bag. I'm so scared they’ll talk behind my back about how useless their senior is.

I just got an email saying I won the department merit scholarship, and my stomach dropped. There must have been a clerical error in the admin office because my DSA lab scores were average, and I only got an S-grade in math because of relative grading. I'm terrified of replying to the email to claim it because what if they check my transcripts again and realize they sent it to the wrong person? I feel like I'm stealing money from someone who actually worked hard.

I finally got placed at an 8 LPA product role, which is huge for my family. But when my dad called our relatives, my uncle bragged about how his son got a 22 LPA package at a fintech firm, and my dad’s voice just went flat. Now I feel like my achievement is absolute garbage and I only got this job because the company was desperate. I worked so hard for months, but now I feel like a complete failure who couldn't even make his parents proud.

I somehow cleared the off-campus interview for a top tech firm, but honestly? It was a fluke. The interviewer was just tired and asked me a basic linked list question while my batchmates got grilled on hard DP problems. Now I'm sitting in this DSA coding lab sweating because my professor expects me to lead the group project, and I know the second I open my editor, everyone is going to realize I can barely write a clean DFS without looking at StackOverflow.

My parents just posted my 9.2 CGPA scorecard on the family WhatsApp group and all my relatives are praising me like I’m some prodigy. I feel like throwing up. I didn’t actually 'learn' anything—I just stayed up on Red Bull cramming ten years of past papers the night before the midterms, and now I’m terrified that when placements start, some interviewer will ask me a basic system design question and I'll just freeze like a total fraud.

I was nominated as the technical lead for our campus coding club, but I swear it’s only because I’m polite and easy to talk to, not because of my skills. There are guys in my batch who write compilers for fun and contribute to Linux, while I spent three hours yesterday debugging a silly NullPointerException. Every time I have to assign tasks, I feel this crushing panic that they're looking at me thinking, 'Why is this idiot in charge of us?'

I got my offer letter yesterday for a high-paying analyst role, but instead of celebrating, I’ve been staring at the ceiling feeling absolute dread. During the final round, I completely fumbled the SQL query and the interviewer basically guided me to the answer out of pity. I’m convinced HR made a clerical error in the selection list and they’re going to realize their mistake during the pre-joining training benchmark exams next month.

After clearing my math backlog, I finally got into the advanced machine learning elective, but walking into that class feels like trespassing. Everyone is talking about their papers published in IEEE and their summer research fellowships at IIT, while I'm just trying to remember basic calculus concepts. I feel like an uninvited guest sitting at a high-table, just waiting for the professor to call on me and expose how far behind I actually am.

I just got selected for the software engineering role at my dream company and I'm literally hyperventilating in the bathroom. Everyone is congratulating me on the placement group, but I know it's a complete fluke—the interviewer literally asked me the only two Leetcode medium questions I had memorized the night before. If he had asked me to explain something basic like polymorphism in-depth, I would have stuttered and failed right there. I feel like an absolute fraud who just cheated the system, and I'm terrified that when I join, they'll realize I can barely write a clean script and fire me on day one.

I got my midterm papers back today and I scored top of the class in Systems Design, but I feel like throwing up. I didn't actually learn anything; I just crammed the previous five years' question banks and parroted back what the professor wanted to see. My friends are asking me for doubts, and every time I explain a concept, I feel like a massive liar who's about to be exposed. I'm not smart, I'm just good at passing exams, and the thought of the upcoming lab exams makes me want to disappear because there's no way to fake actual coding.

I'm doing a group project for our Web Dev lab, and my partners are absolute wizards who discuss Docker and Kubernetes like it's basic English. I sat there in silence during our meet, nodding along because I didn't want them to know that I spent three hours yesterday just trying to configure my CSS grid properly. They gave me a minor UI module to build, and I'm paralyzed because I know whatever I write is going to look like trash next to their backend architecture. I don't belong in this department; the admissions committee made a huge mistake letting me in.

My relative called today to brag that his son got a 30 LPA package, and my mom immediately looked at me with this heavy, silent disappointment. I worked my ass off to secure an 8 LPA offer at a local consulting firm, which I thought was great, but now I feel like an absolute loser who settled for scraps. My parents keep asking me why I didn't apply for the off-campus product roles, but the truth is I was too scared of failing the initial coding rounds. I feel like a massive disappointment who's just pretending to be an engineer.

Every time I draft an announcement for the Discord server, my hands shake because I know the sophomore members are probably way better coders than I am. I want to step down, but the shame of quitting feels just as bad as the shame of being exposed as an incompetent leader.
